d3d.z_compare.text: The z-buffer compares with the {mode} test

debrief.ai_team_counted.text: Player flight group {fg}, which no human flies, entered team {team} in the debriefing's standings as a team of computer pilots; {teams} teams now take part

debrief.battle_counted.text: The battle's results through step {index} were counted: {imperial} Imperial victories, {rebel} Rebel victories and {draws} draws, where {needed} victories end the battle

debrief.campaign_finished.text: Campaign {mission} was marked finished in faction {faction}'s single-player records

debrief.closed.text: The debriefing screen closed: it let go of the mission list ({list}: 1 when one was held) and the campaign debriefing text ({text}: 1 when held), with its background picture and scroll controls

debrief.cursor_placed.text: The pointer was placed over the left button, or over the continue button when {exit} was 0 (a single player or the host in a tournament, battle or campaign that goes on)

debrief.disconnected.text: This player had been dropped from the network game during the mission; the debriefing shut its network session down and told the player

debrief.evaluation.text: The training mission's evaluation award level {award} (1 best to 5, 6 failed, 0 none) picked debriefing picture {result} (1 an award, 2 failed, 0 none)

debrief.fly_again.text: The {kind} mission was to be flown again ({by}); the debriefing left for its setup, or with a single mission straight for flight loading with its last results cleared

debrief.host_aborted.text: The host had aborted the mission; the debriefing told this player it was still connected to the game session

debrief.host_asked.text: The host sent every player the request {request}; it carried {seed}, which every machine takes as the next flight's random seed (0 when it carries none)

debrief.kill_list_full.text: The overview's {list} list already held 8 entries when flight group {fg} was placed in it, so combatant {combatant} (under 8 a network entry, else 8 plus a flight group) fell off its end

debrief.kill_order.text: The overview's kill lists were set: killed {killed} and killed by {killed_by} (under 8 a network entry, 8 and over 8 plus a flight group, -1 ends the list)

debrief.list_missing.text: The debriefing had no mission list for mission type {directory} (the list's loading said why); the 1997 code goes on to read the missing list for the mission's title and for a battle's or campaign's saved progress

debrief.local_pilot.text: The local player holds pilot result entry {entry} (8 when no entry holds it), flying flight group {fg} (-1 with no entry)

debrief.local_pilot_missing.text: No pilot result entry held the local player's id (session mode {mode}); the 1997 code went on to read the entry past the table for the player's flight group

debrief.local_place_missing.text: The pilot's team {team} was not found in the debriefing's order of {teams} teams, so the player statistics page showed its place as first

debrief.melee_result.text: The melee's debriefing picture was picked from tournament result {tournament} and melee result {melee} (1 an award, 2 failed, 0 none; at a tournament's end a team tied for the top score also counts 1)

debrief.mission_listed.text: The debriefing looked for entry {mission} in the mission list of mission type {directory} and stopped at place {index} of {missions} (the place equals the count when the entry was not found)

debrief.next_mission.text: The {kind} went on to its next mission, step {index} counted from 0 ({by}), with {players} human players recorded; the debriefing left for the next mission's setup

debrief.not_listed.text: Entry {mission} was not in the mission list of mission type {directory}, which holds {missions} entries; the 1997 code went on to read the place past the list's end for the mission's title and for a battle's or campaign's saved progress

debrief.opened.text: The debriefing opened for mission {mission} of mission type {directory} (sequence active {sequence}; session mode {mode}: 2 solo, 3 network client, 4 network host) on page {page} (0 overview, 1 player statistics, 2 the sequence's page); dropped from the network game {disconnected}

debrief.order.text: The debriefing's order was set: teams {team_order}, tournament standings {standings_order}, network entries {player_order} (-1 ends each list), standings flags by team {standing_flags}; the pilot's team at position {position}; pilots ranked one by one {by_pilot}; computer opponents {ai_opponents}, session mode {mode}, {groups} flight groups

debrief.outcome.text: The debriefing showed the mission's outcome: the pilot's team {team}; mission complete for the first two teams {completed}; campaign mission complete {campaign} (-1 outside a campaign); award levels for melee, tournament, evaluation and battle {awards} (1 best to 5, 6 failed, 0 none); rank change {promotion} (1 promoted, -1 demoted) at rating {rating}; mission score {score}

debrief.outcome_text_no_buffer.text: The campaign's debriefing text for mission {mission} of mission type {directory} was not read: its 4096-byte buffer was never allocated, so the text page stayed blank

debrief.outcome_text_open_failed.text: The mission file {file} did not open, so the campaign's debriefing text was left empty

debrief.outcome_text_read.text: The campaign's debriefing text was read from mission file {file}: 4096 bytes starting at {offset} from its end, the text for a completed mission: {win}

debrief.outcome_text_skipped.text: Mission file {file} has format {version}, not 14, so it holds no debriefing text and the campaign's text was left empty

debrief.outcome_text_unlisted.text: Mission {mission} of mission type {directory} was not among the {missions} missions of the loaded list, so the campaign's debriefing text was left empty

debrief.packet_ignored.text: The debriefing received a {kind} message and stayed open, acting on nothing (a session cancel or a team list only set a flag nothing reads; a return to setup skipped drawing that one frame)

debrief.page_changed.text: The player turned the debriefing to page {page} (0 the mission overview, 1 the player statistics, 2 the campaign text or the tournament or battle summary) from page {previous}

debrief.page_kept.text: The debriefing's mission type {directory} is none of the six types, so it kept page {page} from the last debriefing

debrief.pilot_result.text: The pilot scored {score} points; rank change {rank_change} (1 promoted, -1 demoted, 0 none), rating now {rating}; this mission's awards in faction record {faction}: melee plaque {plaque}, tournament trophy {trophy}, mission evaluation {evaluation}, battle medallion {medallion} (0 none, 1 the best, an evaluation of 6 a failed one)

debrief.player_counted.text: Network entry {entry}, player {player} (rating {rating}), flying flight group {fg} for team {team}, was counted for the debriefing: score {score}, {kills} full, {shared} shared and {assists} assisted kills, {losses} craft lost, left the flight {has_left}; {teams} teams with a human player and {humans} human players so far

debrief.player_readied.text: The debriefing asked the session roster to mark network entry {entry}, player {player}, ready; the player had left the flight: {has_left}

debrief.progress_ended.text: The {kind} {mission} was over, so the pilot's record no longer offers to continue it ({role}): last step {index}, score {score}

debrief.progress_recorded.text: The {kind} {mission} was not over, so its progress was written into the pilot's record (it reaches disk at the pilot's next save) to continue later ({role}): step {index}, score {score}, marked to continue {active} (1 yes), random seed {seed}

debrief.ready_cleared.text: A ready message from player {player} reached the debriefing, which cleared that player's ready mark at roster place {index}

debrief.results.text: The debriefing ranked {teams} teams with {humans} human players for mission type {directory}: team {top} came first; the pilot's team {team} completed the mission: {completed}, with {score} points

debrief.standing_counted.text: Team {team} went into the tournament standings with {total} points over the tournament and {place1} first, {place2} second and {place3} third places; the mark of the team its computer pilots copy was {ai_source} (0 when none)

debrief.stats_counted.text: The player statistics page recounted itself for network entry {entry} (0 in a solo game): {rows} rows; {kills} full and {shared} shared kills and {assists} assists; kills of human pilots {player_kills} full and {player_shared} shared, of computer pilots {ai_kills} full and {ai_shared} shared; {losses} craft lost, {lost_to_players} to human and {lost_to_ai} to computer pilots; sections shown: kills by craft type {by_type}, kills by rank {by_rank}, losses to players {from_players}

debrief.stats_local_missing.text: The player statistics page found no entry for the local player among the mission's network players, whose player ids were {ids}, in session mode {mode}, and drew only its title

debrief.stats_scrolled.text: The player scrolled the player statistics page to row {row} from row {previous}, of {rows} rows

debrief.team_result.text: Team {team} went into the debriefing's team order: mission completed {completed}, score {score}, {kills} full and {shared} shared kills, {losses} craft lost, completion time {seconds} seconds; computer pilots only {ai_only}; in the tournament standings {in_standings}

debrief.text_alloc_failed.text: The {bytes}-byte buffer for the campaign mission's debriefing text was missing because memory could not be allocated, so the debriefing's text page stayed empty

dialog.confirm_shown.text: The confirm dialog showed {line1} / {line2} / {line3}, with an OK label {ok} and a Cancel label {cancel} (1 set; with neither, a lone OK button)

dialog.network_dismissed.text: A waiting network message closed the confirm dialog after {frame} menu frames, answered as Cancel (the network line before it names the message)

dialog.pilot_name_empty.text: Create Pilot was pressed (the button, Enter or Tab) with no name typed, {frame} menu frames into the prompt; the prompt stayed open

display.clear_failed.text: A display surface was not cleared to black (code {result}); it may still show old pixels

display.drawing_mode.text: Software drawing was set up for resolution mode {mode}: pixel mode {pixel_mode} (0 for 8-bit 320x240, 1 for larger 8-bit, 2 for 16-bit) at {bpp} bits per pixel; graphics detail preset {preset}

display.exclusive_lost.text: A flip found the display out of exclusive full-screen mode; the game took exclusive mode back, flipped again and returned to the normal level

display.flip_timing.text: Flips were lined up with the display's refresh, at a refresh rate scale of {rate} (the display's frequency, or one measured over 100 refreshes)

display.lock_failed.text: Locking the {surface} for drawing failed with code {result}; the lock count was left raised at {count} (always 1 here: a lock is tried only when none is held), and drawing went on through the last locked surface's pixel pointers

display.menu_backup_alloc_failed.text: The {bytes}-byte copy of the menus' offscreen picture could not be allocated (at {site}: start, or after_flight); the menus went on without it, so that picture is neither saved nor put back

display.menu_clear_failed.text: The menus' {surface} was not cleared (code {result}); it may still show old pixels

display.menu_driver_file_short.text: video.cfg opened but did not hold a whole display driver id; the menus used the default display driver

display.menu_lock_failed.text: Locking the menus' {surface} for drawing failed with code {result}. The back buffer was then marked locked anyway and drawing went on through the pointer its last lock gave (when there was none, the game stops); after a failed offscreen lock, drawing stayed on the back buffer

display.menu_present_failed.text: Copying the menu frame to the screen failed with code {result}; the frame was not shown, and the offscreen picture was not put back nor the back buffer cleared for the next frame

display.menu_rebuilt.text: After the flight the menu display was set up again at 640x480 and {bpp} bits per pixel: page flipping {flip} (0 when the back buffer is copied to the screen instead), 5-5-5 pixels {format555} (0 for 5-6-5; 1 also at 8 bits), rows of {back_pitch} bytes in the back buffer and {offscreen_pitch} in the offscreen surface, a palette made {palette}

display.menu_setup_failed.text: Setting up the menu display failed at step {stage} (0 creating DirectDraw, 1 the cooperative level, 2 the 640x480 display mode, 3 the screen surface, 4 the back buffer, 5 the offscreen surface, 6 loading the size-20 font); an error box said so and the menu display was shut down

display.menu_shutdown.text: The menu display shut down: the saved pictures under the screens still stacked (stack level {depth}) were freed with the fonts, images, sound tables and menu text; DirectDraw was still open {direct_draw}, the menu surfaces were still there {surfaces} (0 after a flight took them and they were not rebuilt), and closing the window was asked {destroy} (this version only lets go of the window)

display.menu_started.text: The menu display was set up at 640x480 and {bpp} bits per pixel: page flipping {flip} (0 when the back buffer is copied to the screen instead), 5-5-5 pixels {format555} (0 for 5-6-5; 1 also at 8 bits), rows of {back_pitch} bytes in the back buffer and {offscreen_pitch} in the offscreen surface, a palette made {palette}; a display driver named in video.cfg {configured}, DirectDraw made on that driver {secondary}; one menu frame every {frame_ms} ms

display.menu_surfaces_lost.text: A menu drawing surface was found lost, so the screen surface was restored and, when that worked, the back buffer (or, with page flipping, the offscreen surface); a failure that followed is told on its own line

display.menu_surfaces_released.text: Before the flight the menus let go of their display surfaces: the screen surface {screen_surface}, the palette {palette}, the offscreen surface {offscreen} and the separate back buffer {back_buffer} (1 for each one there to release); DirectDraw and the window were kept

display.mode_refused.text: The display refused the {width}x{height} mode at {bpp} bits per pixel (code {result}); other sizes and pixel depths were tried next

display.overlay_copy_failed.text: Copying the cockpit and HUD layer onto the frame failed with code {result}; the frame went on without it

display.palette_missing.text: No palette could be made for the 8-bit full-screen display, so its colors stayed ones the flight did not choose

display.palette_set.text: {count} palette colors from entry {first} were sent to the display: full screen {fullscreen}, a DirectDraw palette present {palette} (at 0 the 1997 VGA path, which the modern build skips); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

display.present_failed.text: Copying the finished frame to the screen failed at the {step} with code {result}; the frame was not shown

display.resolution_set.text: Flight drawing was set up for resolution mode {mode}: {width}x{height} pixels, {pitch} bytes a row, projection scale {scale} (a shift of {shift}), screen banks of {page} bytes

display.resolution_unknown.text: Resolution mode {mode} is not one the flight knows, so drawing was set up for 320x240

display.setup_failed.text: Setting up the flight display failed at {call} with code {result}, for the {width}x{height} size asked for at {bpp} bits per pixel (for display_mode, the last depth tried, and the code is the last refusal); the game then reported that the flight could not start

display.started.text: The flight display started: full screen {fullscreen}, {width}x{height} at {bpp} bits per pixel (pixel format {format}: 8, 555 or 565), a back buffer to flip {back_buffer} (0 when frames are copied to the screen), hardware 3D {hardware3d}

display.surface_lost.text: A display surface was found lost during the {where} (flip, or overlay: the copy of the cockpit layer onto the frame); restoring the screen surface worked: {restored} (1 yes, 0 no); nothing was drawn again for this frame

display.surfaces_restored.text: The retried flip found the display's surfaces lost; the screen, back buffer and z-buffer were restored and the flip tried once more

display.unlock_unbalanced.text: Drawing was unlocked with no lock held (lock count {count}); the count was set back to 0

files.fatal.text: A file operation failed and the program exits: {message} ({path})

flight.action_key.text: The simulation step applied action key {key} for player slot {slot}: craft object {object} (-1 for none), map view state {map} (0 in the cockpit), hyperspace phase {hyper} (0 when not jumping), open request {request} (0 for none); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.beam_switched.text: Player slot {slot} switched its beam of type {beam} (1 tractor, 2 jamming, 3 decoy, 4 energy transfer) on: {on}, with {charge} charge; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.chat_opened.text: Player slot {slot} started typing a message to its team; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.clock_second.text: The mission clock counted a second at tick {tick}: {elapsed} seconds of mission time, {left} seconds left of a {limit}-minute limit (0 and 0 with no limit); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.component_selected.text: Player slot {slot} picked part {component} of target object {target} to aim at; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.confirm_asked.text: Player slot {slot} was asked to confirm request {request} (2 leave, 3 call reinforcements) with Space within {timer} ticks; the request's object is {param} (-1 for none); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.cooperative_level_failed.text: Setting DirectDraw's {mode} cooperative level failed with code {result}

flight.countermeasure_used.text: Player slot {slot} used countermeasure type {cm} (1 chaff; any other launches a flare): {ammo} left, chaff cover for {seconds} seconds; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.craft_aborted.text: Player slot {slot} sent the computer-flown craft in object {target} home, so it counts as having aborted its mission: flight group {fg} now has {aborted} aborted craft, its special cargo aborted {special}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.craft_jump_unbound.text: Player slot {slot} gave up craft object {previous} to jump to another craft, but no craft took the player, who was left without one

flight.craft_jumped.text: Player slot {slot} jumped from craft object {previous} to craft object {object} (-1 when no craft took the player); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.craft_ordered.text: Player slot {slot} gave the {command} order to the computer-flown craft in object {target}: its plan is now {plan} and the plan it goes back to {saved}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.detail_preset.text: Graphics detail preset {preset} was applied: detail distance {distance}, star grid divisor {stars}, backdrops {backdrops}, debris {debris}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.display_cleanup.text: Flight start failed with error {error}; the display surfaces are released

flight.dock_bonus.text: Player slot {slot} earned points for bringing craft object {object} home in a wave mission: its mission score is now {score}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.ejection_tumble.text: The craft object {object} that player slot {slot} ejected from began to roll at {tumble}, a random rate halved until its model allows it, and to break up for 472 ticks; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.end.text: The flight ends ({reason}); result {result}, where 1 commits the mission results

flight.flip_failed.text: Flipping the flight display failed with code {result}

flight.frames_end.text: The frame loop ended at game tick {tick}: {reason}

flight.hyperspace_aborted.text: Player slot {slot} called off the hyperspace jump of craft object {object} while it was still starting; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.hyperspace_effect_started.text: The hyperspace effect began on this screen for the local player, slot {slot}: the entry sound for side {iff} played (1 is the Imperial sound, any other side gets the other one) and new streaks were placed at random, {count} of them drawn each frame (1,024 with 3D hardware, 512 without); the jump's second stage was {ticks} ticks in (250 make a second)

flight.hyperspace_effect_stretched.text: The hyperspace streaks on this screen reached full length for the local player, slot {slot}, and the exit sound for side {iff} played (1 is the Imperial sound), {ticks} ticks into the jump's second stage (the stretch starts at 472; the effect is drawn until 531)

flight.hyperspace_stalled.text: Craft {object} of flight group {fg} was entering hyperspace with no working systems; it slowed to a stop and became an ordinary craft again; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.laser_link_set.text: Player slot {slot} set laser bank {bank} to fire mode {link} (1 single, 2 dual, 3 all linked); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.lasers_to_shields.text: Player slot {slot} moved {kind} of its laser charge to the shields in steps of {step} energy: {left} charge units were not moved; the shields now hold {front} front and {rear} rear against {limit} a bank, distribution {mode} (0 forward, 1 even, 2 aft); when {kind} is all, the 1997 code then adds one more transfer step to the shields even if the lasers were empty, with no limit check; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.maneuver.text: Computer-flown craft {object} reached a steering stage: {stage}, at angle {angle} (65,536 to a full turn); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.map_entered.text: Player slot {slot} opened the map view and handed its craft to the computer pilot (with its flight group's orders: {ai}); target {target}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.map_left.text: Player slot {slot} closed the map view to fly craft object {object} again; map state {map} (0 back in the cockpit; otherwise no craft was free and the map stayed open); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.map_view_set.text: Action key {key} moved the map view of player slot {slot}: map state {map}, camera on object {focus} and aimed at object {aim} (65,535 for none), {distance} away, at {x} {y} {z}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.mission_ending.text: The mission was set to end at tick {tick}: {reason}; the player slot that decided it was {slot} (-1 when no single player did)

flight.music_track.text: Music track {track} started ({reason}) and runs {ms} ms; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.options.text: Options and taunts are agreed for {players} players under mission cookie {cookie}

flight.order_given.text: Player slot {slot} gave its computer-flown wingmen the {command} order about object {target} (-1 when no craft was found); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.overdrive_switched.text: Player slot {slot} switched its engine overdrive: on {on} (it stays off when the lasers hold no charge); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.phase.text: The flight task moved from phase {from} to phase {to}

flight.player_departed.text: Player slot {slot} (player {player}), already out of the mission, left the game: this machine's player {local}, the host {host}; {players} players remain active; at tick {tick}

flight.player_docked.text: Player slot {slot} brought craft object {object} of flight group {fg} into the hangar of object {hangar}; it now flies craft object {next} (-1, or the same object, when no craft was left), taking part {state} (1 still flying, 2 out of the mission); at tick {tick}

flight.player_ejected.text: Player slot {slot} ejected from craft object {object}, which began to break up; the player who had done the craft the most damage was {by} (-1 when not a player); at tick {tick}

flight.player_quit.text: Player slot {slot} (player {player}) quit the mission; {players} players were flying, this one included; it lost {penalty} points for leaving a melee early; at tick {tick}

flight.players_counted.text: Players taking part were recounted: {active}; participation by slot {states} (0 not in the flight, 1 flying, 2 out of the mission); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.preset_recalled.text: Player slot {slot} took its throttle and power settings from preset {preset} (0 for the first): throttle {throttle} (65,535 is full power), recharge levels {laser_level} for the lasers, {shield_level} for the shields and {beam_level} for the beam; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.preset_saved.text: Player slot {slot} saved its throttle and power settings to preset {preset} (0 for the first): throttle {throttle} (65,535 is full power), recharge levels {laser_level} for the lasers, {shield_level} for the shields and {beam_level} for the beam; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.proving_grounds_key_dropped.text: In the proving grounds, action key {key} of player slot {slot} was dropped: the targeting keys do nothing there; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.quit_penalty.text: Player slot {slot} of team {team} paid 2,000 points for leaving a melee early: its mission score is now {score} and its team's {team_score}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.recharge_set.text: Player slot {slot} set its {system} recharge to level {level} (0 sends all of that power to the engines, 4 is the most); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.reinforcements_called.text: Player slot {slot} called reinforcements for team {team}, at a cost of 5,000 bonus points (the team's bonus score is now {score}); at tick {tick}

flight.request_accepted.text: Player slot {slot} answered request {request} (1 attack my target or the incoming warhead, 4 ignore my target, 5 cover me, 6 head home, 7 wait, 8 go ahead, 9 evade) from player slot {by} (65,535 for the game's own warhead warning), about object {param} (requests 6 to 9 keep an earlier value): its target is now {target} (-1 for none; on requests 4 and 9 the old target stays when no craft is found) and its throttle {throttle} (65,535 is full power, -1 without a craft); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.request_expired.text: Player slot {slot}'s pending request {request} (1 the warning of a warhead fired at the craft; the others a request or order waiting for the player's answer), naming object {param}, ran out of time and was cleared; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.request_posted.text: Player slot {slot} was given request {request} (1 attack my target, 4 ignore my target, 5 cover me, 6 head home, 7 wait, 8 go ahead, 9 evade) by player slot {by}, to answer with Space within {timer} ticks; the request's object is {param} (requests 6 to 9 do not set it and keep an earlier value); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.resupply_called.text: Player slot {slot} called the resupply craft in object {target}, on boarding plan {plan}, to its own craft; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.sfoils_switched.text: Player slot {slot} moved its S-foils: state {foils} (2 set while closing or closed, 1 set while moving); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.shields_distributed.text: Player slot {slot} set its shield distribution to {mode} (0 forward, 1 even, 2 aft), leaving {front} front and {rear} rear; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.shields_to_lasers.text: Player slot {slot} moved shield energy to the lasers: {removed} energy came off the shields, which now hold {front} front and {rear} rear (distribution {mode}: 0 forward, 1 even, 2 aft), dealt round the laser slots as {units} charge units at {step} energy each; the lasers had room for {room} units, and units past that room or dealt to a full slot are lost; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.speed_matched.text: Player slot {slot} matched the speed of target object {target}: the target flew at {speed} against this craft's top speed of {max_speed} after a power margin of {margin} recharge levels, so the throttle became {throttle} (65,535 is full power); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.start.text: The frame loop starts with the local player in slot {local} of {players}

flight.start_failed.text: The flight could not start (error {error}); the 1997 game showed a message box here

flight.sync_ack.text: Slot {slot} answered in pre-flight phase {phase}; {count} answers so far

flight.sync_timeout.text: The pre-flight {stage} wait ran out in phase {phase} with {count} of {expected} answers; the flight does not start

flight.system_repaired.text: System {system} of craft {object}, flown from player slot {slot}, was repaired; its working systems are now {working} (hex); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.system_repairing.text: System {system} of craft {object}, flown from player slot {slot}, has {left} seconds of repair left; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

flight.target_cleared.text: Player slot {slot} cleared its target; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

frontend.pilot_required.text: The player picked {choice} on the top bar from screen context {context} with no pilot selected; a dialog asked for one

frontend.quit_confirmed.text: The player confirmed quitting the game from screen context {context} (0 the concourse or a network screen, 1 mission setup, 4 the debriefing; session mode {mode}, a game in progress: {session}); the other players were told where needed, the options were written and the network session closed

hud.cockpit_lfd_read.text: Cockpit picture file {file} was read: {entries} parts (the picture, its viewport mask and its palette), {bytes} bytes kept (2 fewer when the first part is a palette); predicted world {predicted} (1 when the world comes from steps that are run again later)

hud.cockpit_loaded.text: The cockpit of this machine's player, slot {slot}, flying craft type {craft} (model {model}), was loaded for the flight: cockpit {cockpit}, its view and instrument layouts and the pictures its views start with

hud.digit_count_invalid.text: A number on the flight display, {value}, was to be drawn in {count} places, more than the 5 the digit table holds (6 or more divide by zero; 8 or more first read past the table)

hud.lock_indicator.text: The lock light and targeting tone of this machine's player, slot {slot}, changed to state {state} from {from} (-2 after the HUD was reset): with cannons selected (mode {mode} 0) 4 means a cannon due to fire would hit the target and 0 that none would; with warheads (mode 1) 1 means no target or no lock, 2 locking and 3 locked; target {target} (-1 for none), warhead lock {lock} (0 none, 1 locking, 2 locked)

hud.message_advanced.text: The next waiting message, {message} (pane type {type}), took the ready pane and was shown ({shown} times so far), with {waiting} more still waiting; the pane keeps it {ticks} ticks (354 while others wait, 250 make a second); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

hud.pane_expired.text: The {pane} pane's message {message} (1 for the system and flight group panes, which keep no number once shown), shown {shown} times and {age} seconds in the pane, ran out of time or was cleared after a view change (forced {forced}: above 0 for a view change); the ready pane then shows the next waiting message, if any, else the pane is emptied; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

hud.panel_sprites_read.text: The cockpit's panel sprites were read: {sprites} sprites into the sprite table from entry {first}, passing over the file's first {start} ({records} read in all)

hud.radar_full.text: A radar of this machine's player, slot {slot}, reached its limit of 47 blips: {fore} blips ahead and {aft} behind; objects past the 47th on a radar were left off it (exactly 47 objects reads the same way)

hud.ready_queue_full.text: The ready message queue was full, so waiting message {message}, the last of {waiting} in line, was dropped to make room for a newer one

hud.threat_changed.text: The threat lights of this machine's player, slot {slot}, changed, or were drawn again after the cockpit view was set up: under attack {attack} (1 while a computer craft attacks it with linked lasers, or another player hit it in the last 5 seconds or aims lasers at it from close by), turret lasers aimed at it {laser}, beam on it {beam} (the beam's type, 0 for none)

hud.view_rebuilt.text: The cockpit of this machine's player, slot {slot}, was set up for view {view}, coming from view {from}: cockpit picture {image}, mirrored {mirrored}; instrument set {set} (0 the cockpit, 144 the HUD alone, 288 the craft list); a flight viewport of {width} by {height} pixels with the picture's center moved {offset} rows; MFD pages {active} and {secondary} shown (65535 for none), {saved_active} and {saved_secondary} kept for the way back to the cockpit; page states {states} (scoreboard, goals, message log, damage, hostile craft, friendly craft, map help, unused: 1 open, 0 closed, -2 closing, -1 reopened); predicted world {predicted} (1 when the world comes from steps that are run again later)

options.menu_music.text: Menu music was turned {on} (1 on: CD track 7 started at CD volume {cd_volume} of 65,535; 0 off: the CD track stopped and the volume shown is 0) by {reason} (switched: the sound page's menu music switch; volume: the music volume slider while menu music played, so only the CD volume changed; defaults: Restore defaults on the sound page while menu music was off)

options.opened.text: The configuration screen opened, in session mode {mode} (0 none, 2 solo, 3 network client, 4 network host)

options.page_changed.text: The configuration screen switched from page {from} to page {page} (0 network, 1 single-player video, 2 multiplayer video, 3 sound, 5 taunts)

options.rate_rounded.text: The server update rate {rate} is odd, and the network page offers only 4, 6 and 8: drawing the page as host or in a solo game changed it to {to}

options.restore_answered.text: The Restore defaults question on configuration page {page} (0 network, 1 single-player video, 2 multiplayer video, 3 sound, 5 taunts) was answered {result} (1 okay: that page's settings went back to their defaults; 0 cancel)

options.session.text: The session settings at {site} (load: set from the settings in force; write: about to be saved) were: network transport {type} (1 TCP/IP, the only one this version uses), internet play {internet}, server update rate {rate}, random seed {seed}, button help {help}, a game password set {password_set} (the password itself is never logged), {taunts} of the 4 taunts filled in (their text is never logged), and the last pilot's name {last_pilot}

options.settings_requested.text: The configuration screen's joystick button asked for the OpenXvT settings window, from page {page} (0 network, 1 single-player video, 2 multiplayer video, 3 sound, 5 taunts); this version never shows the original joystick page

options.sound.text: The sound settings at {site} (load: set from the settings in force; write: about to be saved) were: exterior sounds {exterior}, cockpit sounds {interior}, engine sound {engine}, menu sounds {menu_sounds}, pilot messages {pilot_msgs} and tactical officer messages {officer_msgs} (0 off, 1 some, 2 all), commander messages {commander_msgs}, special mission messages {special_msgs}, flight music {music}, menu music {menu_music}; volumes from 0 to 9: menu sounds {menu_volume}, exterior {exterior_volume}, cockpit {interior_volume}, engine {engine_volume}, voices {voice_volume}, music {music_volume}; switches are 1 on, 0 off

options.text_entered.text: Enter or Tab finished the {field} field {index} (taunts count 1 to 4, the password 0) on the configuration screen; the field holds text: {filled} (the text itself is never logged)

options.video.text: The video settings of set {multi} (0 single player, 1 multiplayer) at {site} (load: set from the settings in force; write: about to be saved) were: space backdrops {backdrop}, star density {stars} (0 low to 2 high), space debris {debris}, local light sources {lights}, specular highlights {specular}, diffuse lighting {diffuse}, dithering {dither}, texture resolution {textures} (0 low to 2 high), mip-mapping {mipmap} and detail distance {detail} (slider positions 0 to 19), screen resolution {res} (0 320 by 240, 1 512 by 384, 2 640 by 480), view size {window} (0 320 by 240, 1 480 by 360, 2 640 by 480), colors {colors} (0 for 256, 1 for 16-bit), brightness {brightness} (0 to 7), 3D hardware {hardware}, bilinear filtering {bilinear}; switches are 1 on, 0 off

options.window_size_set.text: Video set {multi} (0 single player, 1 multiplayer): the flight view size became {window} (0 320 by 240, 1 480 by 360, 2 640 by 480) because of {reason} (resolution: screen resolution {res} was picked and the view size follows it; clamp: a view size larger than screen resolution {res} was picked and was lowered to it)

options.written.text: The game options were saved to the player's settings file, with the current pilot as the last pilot (at a flight launch, after a flight, when the configuration screen closes, and at quit)

palette.applied.text: The flight palette was applied at brightness scale {brightness_scale} (256 is normal; each brightness step adds 64) for a {bpp}-bit display; at 8 bits its colors were sent to the display, at 16 nothing was sent

palette.colors_set.text: {count} flight palette colors from entry {first} were set; in pixel mode {pixel_mode} (2 for 16-bit color) the matching 16-bit colors were rebuilt too

pilot.achievements_counted.text: The mission achievements page was counted for faction record {faction}: {rows} rows; solo histories {solo_histories} and network histories {network_histories} (training, melee, combat, tournament, battle and campaign rows)

pilot.awards_table_empty.text: The campaign medal table {file} was empty, so the campaign medals page shows only its title

pilot.awards_table_loaded.text: The campaign medal table loaded with {records} records

pilot.awards_table_missing.text: The campaign medal table {file} could not be opened, so the campaign medals page shows only its title

pilot.awards_table_short.text: The campaign medal table ended early after {records} complete records, while reading a record's {part} line (id, main medal, network awards or solo awards); a record cut short keeps campaign id 0 and is not counted

pilot.awards_table_unallocated.text: No memory could be had for the campaign medal table's {count} records, so the campaign medals page shows only its title

pilot.campaign_title_empty.text: Campaign list entry {index} has an empty title; the {page} page's title cut then reads far outside the title (in a 64-bit build about 4 GB past it, which crashes)

pilot.command_line.text: The command line ({length} characters) was read: a pilot name given {named}, a network address given {address} (1 yes; neither text is logged); the modern build always passes an empty line

pilot.create_choices.text: The new pilot's first mission choices were set: training exercise {training} (the pilot, then faction records 0, 1 and 2) and combat engagement {combat} (the pilot, then faction records 0 and 1); 0 where a list did not load

pilot.create_combat_short.text: The combat engagement list held only {count} missions, fewer than three; the new pilot's combat engagement choice was read from past the list's end

pilot.create_file.text: A new pilot takes file number {number}, {path}, the first such name not already used

pilot.created.text: A new pilot was made in file number {number} at the Trainee rank and made the current pilot; the save that writes its files follows

pilot.cutscene_chosen.text: Cutscene {cutscene} of campaign {campaign} was chosen on the cutscene page; its movie plays next

pilot.cutscenes_counted.text: The cutscene page was counted for faction record {faction}: {campaigns} campaigns listed, {rows} rows from the {cutscenes} cutscenes known

pilot.defaults_set.text: A pilot with no expansion file got a new pilot's Trainee rank and training exercise choices {training} (the pilot, then faction records 0, 1 and 2; 0 where a list did not load) before its base game record was read

pilot.delete_answered.text: The question whether to delete the current pilot was answered: delete {accepted} (1 yes, 0 no)

pilot.delete_asked.text: The roster asked whether to delete the current pilot, from the Delete Pilot button {from_button} (1) or the Delete key (0)

pilot.delete_failed.text: The pilot's {kind} file at roster entry {index} could not be removed, so the delete stopped and the pilot stayed loaded (record: nothing was removed; expansion: the base game record was already removed, so the pilot is half deleted); the roster then stops the game

pilot.delete_match.text: The pilot to delete was found at roster entry {index}, base game record file {path}; its expansion file is the same name ending in 2

pilot.delete_unlisted.text: The current pilot was not among the {count} listed pilot files, so no file was deleted; the pilot was still cleared from memory and the roster rebuilt

pilot.deleted.text: The pilot at roster entry {index} was deleted: its base game record and expansion files were removed

pilot.expansion_unreadable.text: The pilot's expansion file could not be read whole ({bytes} bytes expected), so the pilot data was cleared and the load failed

pilot.faction_chosen.text: The pilot record switched to faction record {faction} (0 Rebel, 1 Imperial), restoring that faction's team {team} and mission type {directory}

pilot.faction_unexpected.text: The pilot's current faction record is {faction}, neither Rebel (0) nor Imperial (1), as after a flight in a flight group of a third side; the pilot record pages read that faction's record, and from 3 up the page buttons mark a slot past their eight

pilot.files_missing.text: Neither of the pilot's files could be opened, so no pilot was loaded

pilot.list_clicked.text: Roster entry {index} was clicked; it was another pilot than the current one {other} (1: it is loaded next; 0: nothing is loaded)

pilot.list_failed.text: The saved pilots' {kind} files could not be listed ({by}): at startup no pilot was loaded, the roster then stops the game, and a save falls back to a new file name

pilot.list_file_unreadable.text: A listed pilot file could not be opened and was skipped after {read} names were read; the roster's later names no longer sit at their files' places, so a click, a typed name or a delete acts on another pilot's file

pilot.list_rebuilt.text: The roster was rebuilt from {count} listed pilot files, {names} names read

pilot.load_files.text: Loading pilot file {path}: expansion file read {expansion}, base game record opened {base} (1 yes)

pilot.loaded.text: A saved pilot was loaded ({by}: startup is the last pilot restored when the game started, list a click on the roster, typed a name typed in the roster's field): roster entry {index}, rating {rating}, faction record {faction} (0 Rebel, 1 Imperial), {missions} missions flown, total score {score}

pilot.medals_counted.text: The campaign medals page was counted for faction record {faction}: {campaigns} campaigns listed, {entries} of them shown with a medal record; {solo_awards} solo and {network_awards} network mission awards (those of the last such campaign)

pilot.name_answered.text: The new pilot's name prompt closed with result {result} (1 a name accepted, 0 none); a name was entered {entered} (1 yes; the name itself is never logged)

pilot.name_matched.text: A typed pilot name was looked up among the {count} listed pilots (-1 with no list): matched {matched} (1 yes; the original build never sets it) at roster entry {index} (the count when none matched)

pilot.name_prompted.text: There were no saved pilots, so the roster asked for a new pilot's name

pilot.names_unallocated.text: No memory could be had for the names of the {count} listed pilots, so the roster shows none and a delete removes no file

pilot.page_chosen.text: The pilot record showed page {page} (0 statistics, 1 awards, 2 rating, 3 mission achievements, 4 campaign medals, 5 cutscenes)

pilot.record_base.text: Saving the base game record: the existing record file was found {found} (1: its bytes are kept where the pilot data has no field for them; 0: the save starts from an empty record)

pilot.record_loaded.text: The pilot's base game record was read into the pilot data: rating {rating}, {missions} missions flown, total score {score}, faction record {faction}, {promo} promotion points at this rating, {percent} percent toward the next, last rank change {rank_change} (1 promoted, -1 demoted, 0 none)

pilot.record_missing.text: The pilot's base game record file could not be opened, so the pilot was loaded from its expansion file alone

pilot.record_out_of_range.text: The pilot's base game record holds rating {rating} (0 to 24 expected) or faction record {faction} (0 to 3 expected); the 1997 code uses both unchecked as table indexes on the pilot record pages and in the next flight's statistics

pilot.record_prepared.text: The pilot's base game record was filled for writing: rating {rating}, {missions} missions flown, total score {score}, faction record {faction}, {promo} promotion points at this rating, {percent} percent toward the next, last rank change {rank_change} (1 promoted, -1 demoted, 0 none)

pilot.record_unreadable.text: The pilot's base game record could not be read whole ({bytes} bytes expected) during a {stage}: on a load the load reported failure and kept what the expansion file gave; on a save the save stopped after the expansion file was written, so the two files now disagree and every later save stops the same way

pilot.restore_none.text: No last pilot was recorded in the options, so no pilot was loaded at start

pilot.restore_unlisted.text: The last pilot recorded in the options was not among the {count} listed pilot files, so no pilot was loaded at start

pilot.save_no_pilot.text: No pilot was loaded, so nothing was saved; a flight launch that asked for this save then closes the game

pilot.save_path.text: The pilot is saved to {path} (temporary file {temporary}: 1 only for the temporary save no caller asks for)

pilot.saved.text: The pilot was saved: its expansion file written whole at rating {rating}, {missions} missions flown, total score {score}, faction record {faction}; its base game record is written next, and a failure there has its own error line

pilot.select_failed.text: The pilot at roster entry {index} did not load ({by}); the pilot data was left holding something {partial} (1: what the pilot's expansion file gave, though the load reported failure, so later saves of it can fail; 0: empty, no pilot loaded)

pilot.stats_counted.text: The pilot statistics page was counted for faction record {faction}: {rows} rows, with the sections for kills by craft type {craft}, kills of players by rank {players} and losses to players by rank {losses} (1 shown)

player.awaiting_craft.text: Player slot {slot} lost object {object} and waits for a new craft; it was destroyed by object {source} (-1 none, as when the player ejected), of object type {source_type} (-1 outside the craft slots); the player who did the most damage was {by} (-1 none); watching the map: {map}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.chat_edited.text: Player slot {slot}'s chat line changed ({edit}): it holds {length} characters, for recipients {recipients} (1 the team, 2 the enemies, 3 everyone, 0 closed); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.chat_sent.text: Player slot {slot} sent a chat line of {length} characters to recipients {recipients} (1 the team, 2 the enemies, 3 everyone); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.craft_bound.text: Player slot {slot} (player {player}) took the controls of object {object}, craft type {craft} of flight group {fg}, at tick {tick} ({kind}: same is the craft the player left for the map, next the following craft of its groups after a craft change, replacement a new craft when the last one was gone)

player.craft_bound_state.text: Player slot {slot}'s new craft, object {object} (identity stamp {signature}), took the player's saved settings: throttle {throttle}, shield distribution {distribution} with {front} front and {rear} rear shield energy, target object {target} (-1 none); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.craft_gone.text: Player slot {slot}, waiting for a new craft, found object {object} gone (slot empty: {empty}; else another craft holds it now), so flight group {fg}'s waves were checked before a new craft was sought; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.craft_inspected.text: The player in slot {slot} inspected craft {object} of flight group {fg}, craft type {craft}, the team numbered {order} to inspect it; it carried the special cargo: {special}; at tick {tick}

player.craft_kept.text: Player slot {slot} kept its craft: only {owned} of its craft could fly, and a craft change needs two, so nothing went to the computer pilot; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.craft_release_skipped.text: Player slot {slot} flew no craft, so none went to the computer pilot; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.craft_released.text: Player slot {slot} handed object {object} of flight group {fg} to the computer pilot at tick {tick}; the group's first order was to be applied: {orders} (0 for a plain map view and in a melee); the craft's plan is now {plan}

player.craft_unavailable.text: No craft of player slot {slot}'s flight groups was free to fly (the search started after object {previous}, -1 for the first slot, and asked for identity stamp {preferred}, 0 for any), so the player got no craft; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hangar_offered.text: The player in slot {slot} came within hangar range {range} of craft {mothership} of flight group {fg} and was offered its hangar (mothership choice {pass}: 0 the departure mothership, 1 the alternate); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hyperspace_aligned.text: The craft {object} of player slot {slot} finished turning onto the jump line and entered the second stage of the jump at speed {speed}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hyperspace_blocked.text: The hyperspace jump of player slot {slot} (craft {object}) was called off: object {blocker} (object type {type}) lay {ahead} units ahead in the jump path; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hyperspace_cancelled.text: The hyperspace jump of player slot {slot} (craft {object}) was dropped at stage {phase} because the craft was no longer active (state {state}); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hyperspace_departed.text: The craft {object} of player slot {slot} (craft type {craft}, flight group {fg}) left the battle through hyperspace at tick {tick}, earning {award} points; the player's mission score is now {score}

player.hyperspace_refused.text: Player slot {slot}'s jump to hyperspace was refused ({reason}: an Interdictor or modified strike cruiser of another IFF held it, or the hyperdrive was damaged); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.hyperspace_started.text: Player slot {slot} started the jump to hyperspace in object {object} of flight group {fg} at tick {tick}

player.hyperspace_unavailable.text: Player slot {slot}'s craft had no hyperdrive; the player was pointed to mothership object {departure} and alternate mothership object {alternate} (-1 when not present); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.inspection_counted.text: The player in slot {slot} inspected craft {object} of flight group {fg} for team {team}, the team numbered {order} to inspect it; it carried the special cargo: {special}; the group now counts {count} craft inspected, {team_count} of them by this team, and the player {total}; the inspection scored for the player: {scored}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.map_overview.text: Player slot {slot}'s map camera finished pulling back from object {focus} to the overview, at height {height}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.map_without_craft.text: Player slot {slot}, watching from the map, had no craft left to fly even after flight group {fg}'s waves were checked, so the player left the mission; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.order_ignored.text: Player slot {slot}'s order {command} about object {target} went to no wingman: the object was not hostile to the player's team; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.order_passed.text: Player slot {slot}'s order {command} about object {target} (-1 none) reached {wingmen} wingmen, the last of them object {last} (-1 none); order 155 keeps them away from the object, any other sends them after it; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.out_of_mission.text: Player slot {slot} was out of the mission at tick {tick}; {flying} players were still flying

player.pick_decoyed.text: The object player slot {slot} aimed at, object {target}, was hidden by a decoy beam, so no target was picked; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.quit_flight.text: Player slot {slot} (player {player}) quit the flight: its craft went to the computer pilot, it stopped taking part, and {active} players stayed active; this machine's player: {local}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.release_plan_craft.text: Player slot {slot}'s release of object {object} wrote the order slot and plan to the released craft itself: {same} (0: to another craft, whichever one the game last worked on); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.roll_mode.text: Player slot {slot}'s sideways stick changed to {roll} (1 rolls the craft while the roll key is held, 0 turns it) and the smoothed stick input started over from 0; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.settings_saved.text: Player slot {slot} kept object {object}'s settings for its next craft: throttle {throttle}, recharge levels laser {laser_level}, shields {shield_level} and beam {beam_level}, shield distribution {distribution}, laser link modes {links}, warhead launcher modes {warheads}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.shield_moved.text: Player slot {slot} moved {moved} shield energy into shield bank {shield} (0 front, 1 rear) from the other bank, which now hold {front} front and {rear} rear; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.target_changed.text: Player slot {slot} targeted object {target}, replacing object {previous} (-1 none); chosen in the map view: {map}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.target_component.text: Player slot {slot}'s new target, object {target}, was aimed at its component {component} (0 for an object outside the craft slots); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.target_component_moved.text: The component player slot {slot} was aiming at, component {from} of craft {object}, was destroyed, so the aim moved to component {to} (the same number when no other intact one could be aimed at); predicted step {predicted} (always 0 here)

player.target_dropped.text: Player slot {slot} lost its target, object {target} ({reason}: the slot emptied, the object became an explosion, the player's targeting computer was out, or a decoy beam hid it); the target camera gave way to the forward view: {camera}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.target_refused.text: Player slot {slot} could not target object {target}: its craft's targeting computer was out; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.taunt_sent.text: Player slot {slot} sent taunt {taunt} (0 to 3) to recipients {recipients} (1 the team, 2 the enemies, 3 everyone); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.throttle_stepped.text: Player slot {slot} stepped the throttle by {step}, from {old} to {throttle} (it holds at 0 and 65535); predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.view_focus.text: Player slot {slot}'s view now follows object {focus} (the player's own craft: {own}); outside camera {external}, target camera {target_camera}, view mode {view}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

player.wingman_released.text: Wingman object {object} of player slot {slot} stopped waiting for the go order and went back to its plan {plan}; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

port.host_invalid.text: The runtime needs an initialized 640x480 Aeron host

preview.buffer_alloc_failed.text: The craft preview's {bytes}-byte span mask buffer could not be allocated; the code does not check, and goes on to write the mask through memory handle 0, which holds no block

preview.buffers_ready.text: The craft preview's first draw after a load set up its drawing buffers for a {width}x{height} view, with a span mask buffer of {bytes} bytes

preview.load_failed.text: The craft preview did not load the model {file} ({reason}: extension, the name does not end in .opt; open, the file did not open); the model shown before, if any, stayed on screen

preview.loaded.text: The craft preview loaded the model {file} as memory handle {handle}; its size was taken as {extent} model units, so it was drawn scaled by {scale}

proving.checkpoint_crossed.text: The local player crossed proving grounds gate {checkpoint} on level {level} with {minutes}:{seconds} left: {passed} gates passed, {remaining} to go; predicted step {predicted} (1 in a step that is run again later)

proving.checkpoint_placed.text: Proving grounds gate {checkpoint} (object type {type}) was placed at {x}, {y}, {z}, turned to roll {roll}, pitch {pitch} and heading {yaw}

proving.level_completed.text: Proving grounds level {level} was completed at tick {tick} with {left} seconds left on the clock, worth a bonus of {bonus} points, for a score of {score}, with {targets} targets destroyed so far

proving.level_started.text: Proving grounds level {level} started with {minutes}:{seconds} on the clock and a score of {score} so far, at tick {tick}

proving.target_destroyed.text: On the proving grounds, component {component} of course object {object} was destroyed (a moving one, worth double: {moving}): {targets} targets so far, score {score}, and the clock gained 2 seconds, now {minutes}:{seconds}; predicted step {predicted} (always 0 here)

remaster.alpha_override.text: OPT alpha override for {model} {texture}: mode {mode}, cutoff {cutoff}

remaster.asset_failed.text: Loading an original image or texture asset failed: {error}

remaster.cockpit_art_missing.text: Cockpit view {view} has no prepared resident artwork

remaster.cockpit_prepared.text: Resident cockpit resources were prepared in {ms} ms at {width}x{height}

remaster.config_failed.text: The remaster configuration could not be applied: {error}

remaster.host_missing.text: The modern renderer needs an initialized Aeron host

remaster.opt_gpu_failed.text: OPT {path}: GPU creation failed with status {status}

remaster.opt_init_failed.text: The OPT mesh loader could not be initialized: {error}

remaster.ready.text: The modern renderer is initialized and modern presentation is requested

remaster.stars_gpu_failed.text: The starfield's GPU resources could not be created

render.backdrop_missing.text: Backdrop object type {type} has no loaded image, so drawing it took an image address from outside the game's table of loaded blocks

render.batch_too_large.text: A batch of {vertices} vertices and {triangles} triangles was sent to the 3D card at the {site} flush (mesh: before the next mesh; frame: at the end of the frame), over the {max} vertices its command buffer takes, so its vertices were refused and the batch was not drawn as built

render.billboard_queue_full.text: All 32 places for flat images waiting to be drawn were taken, so frame {frame} of object {object} (an object type for a few callers) was left out of this picture

render.bitmap_too_large.text: A {width}x{height} image is over the 65,536-pixel texture limit and gets no texture

render.bwing_bridge_found.text: The B-wing model's bridge was found as mesh {index}; the B-wing's turning bridge is drawn from that mesh for the rest of the run

render.cockpit_mask_overrun.text: A mirrored row of the cockpit's window outline, {width} pixels wide, took {bytes} bytes to decode, more than the 99 its row buffer holds; the bytes past it were written over other data on the stack

render.color_key_dropped.text: No see-through version of a {width}x{height} model texture could be made for the 3D card (every pixel was see-through, or the upload failed), so the texture was marked and is drawn without one from then on

render.framebuffer_cleared.text: The software frame buffer was cleared and its table of {rows} row offsets built; the radar's target marker was set to {points} points; a frame buffer was there to clear: {present}

render.hardware_unsupported.text: The 3D device lacks an essential feature: z-buffer {z_buffer}, perspective-correct textures {perspective}, hardware {hardware}

render.list_full.text: The list of objects to draw had all 296 entries in use, so object {object} (depth {depth}) was left out of this picture

render.mesh_dropped.text: A mesh of an object of type {type} (-1 for none) was not drawn by the {drawing} renderer because the scene buffers were full: {queued} meshes queued of 500, {faces} faces listed of 5,000 with {mesh_faces} more asked for, a mesh of {mesh_vertices} vertices against room for {vertex_max} and {mesh_edges} edges against room for {edge_max}

render.node_ref_missing.text: A model of object type {type} (-1 for none) refers to a part by a name the model does not hold, so that part was not drawn

render.palette_overrun.text: A texture's converted {bpp}-bit palettes took {colors} colors, but its file kept room for {reserved}; the colors past that were written beyond the texture's memory

render.palette_skipped.text: A texture palette of {colors} colors, over the 1,023 the 16-bit conversion takes, was left unconverted, so image {image} (-1 for the texture's own palette) drew with another image's colors or with memory nothing filled

render.palettes_converted.text: A texture's palettes were converted for {bpp}-bit drawing: {images} images, {colors} colors written after its data

render.projectile_key_cleared.text: A {width}x{height} texture of a projectile (craft class {genus}) had its see-through color mark cleared, so the 3D card draws it with no see-through color from then on
